status: adopted before any official Gate V benchmark run; change only through a new DECISION_LOG entry that names the target, the old and new value and the reason (MASTER_SPEC Part 17 Gate V mandatory note)

machine.cpu: 2 x Intel Xeon Gold 6226, 48 logical CPUs, 2 NUMA nodes; cgroup CPU quota 11.52 CPUs shared with other tenants and about 15 agents
machine.gpu: 1 x NVIDIA RTX A6000, 46,068 MiB, shared with other tenants; governor budget 24,000 MB, 4 GPU jobs at once
machine.numba: not installed (and not to be installed into /venv/main)

units.sim_days_per_cpu_hour: simulated days per CPU-hour of the world process and its children (CPU-seconds, so the load of other tenants does not move it); simulated days per wall hour are reported next to it
units.bytes_per_individual_day: bytes of event log plus batch blobs written per individual (population row) per simulated day, after retention compaction (crucible.substrate.retention.compact)

world: the integrated v5 world: crucible.civ.generate("balanced", seed, population=<profile>) with every subsystem and the one population; the population-only world (crucible.population.worlds.population_world) is measured as a second row and does not satisfy a target

targets.derivation: Gate suites run development-profile worlds; a 30-day run (the shortest Gate P horizon) of one seed must fit in 30 CPU-minutes so that 3 seeds on 3 CPUs plus world generation finish inside the 3,600 s timeout tier of the slow gate tests: 30 days / 0.5 h = 60.
Gate P requires 365-day runs with several seeds; three seeds on three of the nine budget CPUs must finish within 24 wall hours: 365 / 24 = 15.2, rounded down to 15.
Large-civilisation experiments at the 90-day Gate P horizon with three seeds on three CPUs must finish within 24 wall hours: 90 / 24 = 3.75.

The 10M-identity capacity run (V.2: at least 10,000,000 distinct identities with recorded qualifying consumption decisions on the population's columnar path) is one scheduled job: at most 2 wall hours on at most 4 of the 9 budget CPUs, at most one third of the 92.6 GB container RAM (the machine is shared) and at most 5 GB of disk (about a third of the free disk).
Generation must stay below 5% of the shortest research run (a 30-day development run = 30 CPU-minutes = 1,800 s; 5% = 90 s), rounded up to 120 s for the larger profiles.

A 365-day standard run (10,296 individuals x 365 days = 3.76M individual-days) must fit in 2 GB of store so that three seeds and the other tenants' stores fit in the about 14 GB of free disk: 2e9 / 3.76e6 = 532, rounded to 550.

Daily snapshots of a large run must be cheap next to a simulated day (at T3 one simulated day takes 16 CPU-minutes; 60 s is 6%) and small next to the 2 GB per-run disk budget of T6 (500 MB keeps four retained snapshots).

At the large profile 1,000 adaptive participants deciding every 15 minutes make 96,000 decisions per simulated day; at T3 (3.75 days per CPU-hour) that is 360,000 decisions per CPU-hour, and the shared policy may use at most 1% of the CPU budget (36 s): 360,000 / 36 = 10,000 decisions per CPU-second.
The Gate V criterion (ACCEPTANCE_MANIFEST V.4), measured at equal decisions in the integrated world's own class-2 batches and in a backend matrix.
The Gate V criterion (V.5): dense per-tick policy evaluation of every participant versus event-driven activation, with equal recorded outcomes.
The Gate V criterion (V.6), on an integrated workload over three worlds sharing the cache, plus at most one encoder run per artifact (SP-13.5).

At the large profile 20 semantic generalists deciding every 15 minutes with about 40 generated tokens per decision produce 76,800 tokens per simulated day; at T3 that is 80 tokens per second of wall time; 100 leaves headroom. Measured batched (16 requests) on the GPU within a 4,000 MB grant.
Every benchmark job runs under crucible.scale.slots with declared grants in all seven dimensions; no violation may be recorded (Gate V item 8).
